This basically came from the need to be able to boot 32-bit Atom SMP

column2: i.e. a host which doesn't support MOVBE. As a
qemu has since recently received MOVBE support but we

column1: cannot share that with kvm emulation and thus we have to do this in the
host. We're waay faster in kvm anyway. :-)

column2: we piggyback on the #UD path and emulate the MOVBE functionality.
an 8-core SMP guest boots in under 6 seconds.
requesting MOVBE emulation needs to happen explicitly to work
a fairly straight-forward boot of a MOVBE-enabled 3.9-rc6+

column1: kernel in kvm executes MOVBE ~60K times.
